html.p: The SimpleBoxplot dataType lets you plot boxplot distributions directly from a standard Splunk search result table — one row per box, no transposing required. Use dataType=SimpleBoxplot to activate this builder.
The search must return between 6 or 7 columns in this exact order:

tr.td: Label shown on the x-axis for this box

html.p: The option string must define at least xAxis: {} — the builder populates xAxis.data from column 0. Any series defined in the option is preserved; the boxplot series (and optional scatter outlier series) are appended.
To compute the five statistics in Splunk from raw measurements, use:

pre.code: | stats min(cycle_s) AS lower, perc25(cycle_s) AS Q1, median(cycle_s) AS median, perc75(cycle_s) AS Q3, max(cycle_s) AS upper BY workstation | eval outliers=null()

html.p: The search below simulates a quality-control dataset for a production line: five workstations, each with a distribution of per-part cycle times (seconds). Two stations — Assembly and QC-Inspect — have outlier values shown as separate scatter points above the whiskers.

pre.code: | makeresults count=1 | eval station="Welding", lower=38.2, Q1=42.5, median=46.1, Q3=50.8, upper=59.4 | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval station="Assembly", lower=55.1, Q1=61.3, median=65.7, Q3=71.2, upper=82.5, outliers="90.2|95.8"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval station="Paint-Booth", lower=110.4, Q1=118.9, median=124.3, Q3=131.7, upper=145.2] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval station="QC-Inspect", lower=28.6, Q1=33.4, median=37.8, Q3=42.3, upper=52.1, outliers="58.3|63.1|68.7"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval station="Packaging", lower=15.8, Q1=19.2, median=22.4, Q3=26.1, upper=32.7] | table station lower Q1 median Q3 upper outliers

html.p: Note: rows without an outliers field will have a null value for column 6. The builder skips null outlier entries, so no phantom scatter points appear. Always use null() (not empty string) for stations with no outliers.

html.p: Because the builder appends to the existing option.series array, you can pre-populate it with additional series such as a target-time reference line. Declare the line series before the boxplot series and it will appear behind the boxes:

Or add a fixed threshold using markLine directly on the boxplot series via the ECharts option after the builder has run — the builder does not overwrite markLine properties already present in the option template:
The builder detects the template entry (series[0]) and assigns the boxplot data to it, preserving the markLine definition. Outliers are always appended as an additional scatter series.
